points.description: States that excess kurtosis is a difference/subtraction between the distribution's own kurtosis coefficient and the kurtosis coefficient of the normal distribution (i.e. kurtosis minus normal kurtosis, in any wording; stating 'kurtosis minus 3' is acceptable).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only vaguely right: e.g. says it compares kurtosis with a normal distribution, or measures peakedness relative to normal, without clearly stating the difference.

rubric.notes: Full marks for the core idea: excess kurtosis = distribution's kurtosis minus the normal distribution's kurtosis, in any wording. Give 1 mark if the answer only mentions comparison with the normal distribution or peakedness/tailedness relative to normal without the difference. Give 0 for unrelated or wrong definitions.
